technology.summary:
Today's most important technology news includes:
- Anthropic has cut off its internal evaluations from the live internet, as it can't reliably control its AI agents.
- Microsoft 365 Family subscribers will be able to share AI benefits.
- OpenAI has defended its decision to fire three safety researchers.
- Meta has banned ads from TikTok's Chinese parent company ByteDance across the US and several other countries.
- Microsoft has been barred from sponsoring foreign workers for US residency.
- Google's new operating system has had a rocky start, with the software being a weak point.
- Instinct, an AI agent, has become a popular topic in the AI space.
- President Donald Trump has attempted to rebrand AI.

finance.summary: Today's most important finance news includes the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India teaming up to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. This comes as Indian equity benchmarks experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices. A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher. In India, hospital stocks slipped after the Supreme Court highlighted troubling markups on cancer drugs enforced by hospitals.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

In other news, Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC, claiming that his ability to execute illegal orders makes him a liability for the country. Congress has also condemned the detention of tribal students who were heading to Mumbai to protest.

In the US, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process 'corrupt', citing an Indian election that didn't happen. This appears to be a mix-up with the Brazilian election, which took place on Sunday.

Finally, Koel Mallick has joined the BJP, and India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly dropped by $18.34 billion in a single week.
